"'''Thought: A Logical Inquiry'''" is an essay by [[Gottlob Frege]].<ref>Frege, G., 1918. "Thought", in his ''Logical Investigations'', Oxford: Blackwell, 1977</ref> It was published as "Der Gedanke. Eine logische Untersuchung" in the philosophy journal ''Beiträge zur Philosophie des deutschen Idealismus'' (English: Contributions to the philosophy of [[German idealism]]) in 1918. It was republished in ''[[Mind (journal)|Mind]]'' in English in 1956. In it, Frege argues against idealism and for [[platonism]] about thoughts, or [[Proposition|propositions]].<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=DQ_KIHulsoUC&pg=PA3 Thought and Language p. 3]</ref><ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=s9sMEAAAQBAJ The Meaning of Thought]</ref> Frege says ideas are private, but thoughts are public. Frege said that such [[Abstract and concrete|abstract objects]] were members of a '''third realm'''<!--boldface per WP:R#PLA; 'Third Realm (Frege)' redirects here-->.<ref>[[Gottlob Frege]], "Der Gedanke. Eine logische Untersuchung", in: ''Beiträge zur Philosophie des deutschen Idealismus'' 1 (1918/19), pp. 58–77; esp. p. 69.</ref> Frege also argued for a [[redundancy theory of truth]].

Quoting Frege, "The thought, in itself immaterial, clothes itself in the material garment of a sentence and thereby becomes comprehensible to us. We say a sentence expresses a thought."
